violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal and RTE Foods
violations.observation: Raw animal food storage, preparation, holding or display conducted in a manner that may cause cross contamination of ready-to-eat food as follows: RAW CHICKEN ON SHELF ABOVE COOKED NOODLES, LETTUCE IN WIC.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods like poultry, beef, pork, seafood, and eggs from cooked foods, ready-to- eat foods, washed produce, etc during storage, preparation, holding or display. Raw foods shall be stored on shelving units BELOW or SEPARATED from all cooked foods, commercially processed foods, washed produce, leftover foods, etc. CFM HAD EMPLOYEE REARRANGE FOOD IN UNIT. EHS REMINDED CFM THAT COOKED AND READY TO EAT FOODS SHOULD BE STORED ON HIGHER SHELVES IF ON SAME STORAGE UNIT AS RAW PROTEINS.

violations.title: RTE TCS Food Prepared On Site, Date Marking
violations.observation: The following refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food that is prepared on site is not used or discarded within 24 hours of preparation and was not observed to be date marked: GREEN CURRY WITH LABEL 06/29, MASSAMAN CURRY WITH LABEL 7/25.
violations.corrective_action: Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that are prepared on site and kept for more than 24 hours cannot have a shelf-life of more than 7 days, including the day of preparation. These food items must be marked with either the 'consume-by' date and/or 'preparation' date, color-coded labels, or another marking system/method that effectively indicates shelf-life that is clearly understood and properly used by the employees. CFM STATED LABELS HAVE NOT BEEN UPDATED AND CURRIES ARE PREPARED TWICE A WEEK. CFM RELABELLED CONTAINERS WITH CORRECT PREP DATE.

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal and RTE Foods
violations.observation: Raw animal food storage, preparation, holding or display conducted in a manner that may cause cross contamination of ready-to-eat food as follows: RAW SHELL EGGS ON SHELF ABOVE PREPARED FOODS AND VEGETABLES IN WIC.

Raw foods shall be stored on shelving units BELOW or SEPARATED from all cooked foods, commercially processed foods, washed produce, leftover foods, etc. CFM MOVED RAW SHELL EGGS TO BOTTOM SHELF.

out_items.name: Proper reheating procedures for hot holding

violations.title: Reheating for Hot Holding, Proper Temp
violations.observation: The following food item(s) was not reheated for hot holding to a sufficient temperature and/or time: OBSERVED PEANUT SAUCE AT 84F-100F REHEATING IN WARMER.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food that is cooked, cooled, and reheated for hot holding shall be reheated to a minimum temperature of 165F for 15 seconds. EHS HAD CFM MICROWAVE PEANUT SAUCE TO MINIMUM OF 165F. EHS OBSERVED PEANUT SAUCE REHEATED TO 191F.

out_items.name: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures and records

violations.title: TPHC, Food Marked with 4 Hour End Point
violations.observation: The following food item(s) for which time rather than temperature is used as a control is not marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control: COOKED RICE AND WASHED LETTUCE AT EXPO LINE..
violations.corrective_action: If time only, rather than time in accordance with temperature control, up to a maximum of 4 hours, is used as the public health control the food shall: 1) have an initial temperature of 41F or less if removed from cold holding temperature OR 135F or above if removed from hot holding temperature control, 2) be marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control, 3) be cooked and served, served if ready-to-eat, or discarded within 4 hours from the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control, and 4) be discarded if unmarked or marked to exceed a 4 hour limit. 4 HOUR ENDPOINT OF 3:30PM WRITTEN ON COOKED RICE AND WASHED LETTUCE.

out_items.name: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage, and display

violations.title: Food Storage 6 inches above Floor
violations.observation: Food stored on the floor and/or food stored less than 6 inches off the floor. CONTAINERS OF PREPARED FOOD STORED DIRECTLY ON FLOOR OF WIC.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food at least 6 inches off the floor on approved shelving units or dunnage racks. Milk crates, soda crates, or bread racks are not suitable for food storage. CFM WILL WORK ON REARRANGING WIC SO ALL FOODS ARE ON SHELVES. SAKOON THAI (Inspection Date: 02/06/2026) Page 2 of 3

out_items.name: Adequate ventilation and lighting, designated areas used

violations.title: Protective Shielding on Light Bulbs
violations.observation: OBSERVED MISSING CEILING LIGHT COVER IN BACK KITCHEN ABOVE DISH MACHINE.

out_items.name: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use

violations.title: Eating, Drinking, or Using Tobacco
violations.observation: A food employee was observed eating, smoking, or drinking in areas where they may contaminate food, clean equipment, utensils or other items needing protection. Observed food preparation employee eat watermelon while wearing gloves used for food preparation.
violations.corrective_action: Food employees may only eat, drink, or use tobacco in a designated area like a dining room or office area. Employees shall not eat or drink in the kitchen areas, warewashing areas, or storage areas where items may become contaminated. CFM discussed with employee proper procedures for eating. EHS advised CFM to discuss removal of gloves, hand washing and eating in designated area. Food service employee should wash hands and don new gloves when returning from eating and before engaging in food preparation.

out_items.name: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible

violations.title: Paper Towels Provided
violations.observation: Observed that paper towels were not provided at each handwashing sink. No paper towels available at kitchen hand sink or front bar hand sink.
violations.corrective_action: Provide paper towels at each hand sink to allow employees to properly dry their hands after handwashing. CFM provided paper towels.

violations.title: Handwashing Sink, Designated Use
violations.observation: Observed front bar hand sink being used to refill drinking water carafes.
violations.corrective_action: Handsinks are to be used only for washing hands to encourage proper hand washing and to prevent contamination of cleaned hands. EHS discussed with CFM designated hand sink usage. EHS advised CFM to use soda gun to refill water carafes.

out_items.name: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events

violations.title: Clean-up of vomiting and diarrheal events
violations.observation: The food establishment does not have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events.
violations.corrective_action: A food establishment shall have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the food establishment. The procedures shall address the specific actions employees must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of employees, consumers, food and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. EHS TO E-MAIL DOCUMENT.

violations.title: Proper thawing methods used for TCS Foods
violations.observation: Observed the following food thawing using an improper method: two bags of frozen seafood was observed the three compartment sink.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be thawed using one of the following methods: 1) under refrigeration that maintains the food temperature at 41F or less, 2) completely submerged under running water at a water temperature of 70F or below with a sufficient velocity to agitate and float off loose particles of food as long as held for period of time at a temperature of 41F or less, or 3) as part of a cooking process if the food is cooked as specified by Law or thawed in a microwave oven and immediately transferred to a conventional cooking process. EMPLOYEE RELOCATED SEAFOOD TO PREP SINK AND BEGAN RUNNING COOL WATER OVER PRODUCT.

out_items.name: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage, and display

violations.title: Food Storage 6 inches above Floor
violations.observation: Food stored on the floor and/or food stored less than 6 inches off the floor. Packaged duck was observed stored on the floor of the walk in cooler.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food at least 6 inches off the floor on approved shelving units or dunnage racks. Milk crates, soda crates, or bread racks are not suitable for food storage.

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: Dispensing and/or in-use utensils improperly stored between use as follows: scoop used for rice was observed in a container of water.
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently.
